I just don't have any energy or drive to do anything anymore.\n\nDoctor: Do you experience any recurring, distressing thoughts or worries that you can't control, or feel excessively anxious about everyday things or the future?\n\nPatient: No, I don't really have those kinds of anxious worries or racing thoughts. It's more that I just feel completely shut down, empty, and numb inside. It has stayed about the same for a little over two years now.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about how your feelings of emptiness and lack of energy have changed or stayed the same over the past two years, and have you experienced any periods where you felt somewhat better or more like your old self?\n\nPatient: It hasn't changed or gotten any better; it's stayed consistently the same heavy, numb way for a little over two years now. I haven't had any periods where I felt like my old self again. It's just been a constant emptiness ever since that first year.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any significant emotional pain or distress in response to reminders of your husband, or have you had difficulty accepting the loss, in addition to the emptiness and lack of energy you've described?\n\nPatient: It's not really a sharp emotional pain or crying; it's more of a heavy, hollow numbness where I just can't care about anything. But in the evenings, I do hear his voice plain as day calling my name or telling me not to trust people, which scares me so much I just freeze up. Otherwise, I just feel completely empty and devoid of any energy.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about hearing your husband's voice, such as how often it happens and if it's always the same things he's saying?\n\nPatient: I hear his voice most days, usually in the evenings coming from the back bedroom or the garden. He sometimes calls my name or tells me not to trust people at the door, and it's been happening regularly for the past few months. It scares me so much that I just sit there and listen to him instead of answering the phone or the doorbell.\n\nDoctor: Do you believe the voice you hear is really your husband's spirit trying to communicate with you, or do you think it might be something else, like your own mind playing a trick on you?\n\nPatient: It sounds so incredibly real, just like he is actually right there in the back bedroom or out in the garden. Even though I know the room is physically empty, it is so convincing that I honestly don't know what to believe—whether it is his spirit or my mind playing tricks on me. It just scares me so much that I end up just sitting there and listening to him.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any other unusual perceptions, such as seeing things that aren't there or feeling like someone is touching you when no one is around, in addition to hearing your husband's voice?\n\nPatient: No, I've never seen anything that isn't there or felt anyone touching me. It is strictly just hearing my husband's voice, either calling out my name or warning me not to trust the people who come to the door.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever felt like you're doing things or making decisions because the voice you hear is telling you to, or does the voice just scare you without influencing your actions?\n\nPatient: Yes, his voice definitely influences what I do because it makes me too scared to act. I don't have any control over when it happens or what he says. It scares me so much that I just sit there and listen to him.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any other breaks from reality, such as believing things that aren't true or feeling like you're in danger when you're not, aside from hearing your husband's voice?\n\nPatient: No, I don't have any other beliefs like that, and I don't feel like I'm in danger. It's just that his voice tells me not to trust people who come to the door, which scares me so much that I just sit there and ignore the phone or the doorbell.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had any periods where the voice stopped or you didn't hear it for a while, or has it been consistently present over the past few months?\n\nPatient: No, it hasn't stopped at all. I'm not really sure if there are times I'm less likely to hear it, but it mostly occupies my evenings and just scares me into sitting there and listening. It is all just so tiring and frightening.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the voice you hear is something that would go away if you were distracted or engaged in an activity you enjoy, or does it persist regardless of what you're doing?\n\nPatient: I'm not really sure because I can't bring myself to do the activities I used to enjoy anymore. When I do hear his voice, it scares me so much that I just end up sitting there frozen and listening to it, making it impossible to distract myself or even answer the door or phone.\n\nDoctor: Do you think that the voice you hear is a direct result of your grief over your husband's passing, or does it feel like a separate issue that you're experiencing?\n\nPatient: While his voice started after he passed, it really feels like more than just grief now. Reply naturally in English as the Patient to the last Doctor utterance.\nAnswer only the question, in 2–3 sentences maximum.\n\n[Dialogue]\nDoctor: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?\n\nPatient: Since my husband passed, it feels like everything inside me just shut down, and I can’t make myself do the things I used to care about. I just feel so empty and tired, and I don't know how to get going again.\n\nDoctor: Do you often find yourself thinking about your husband and feeling guilty about something related to his passing or your life after he's gone?\n\nPatient: No, I don't really feel guilty about his passing. It's just that since he left, I feel completely empty and shut down inside. I just don't have any energy or drive to do anything anymore.\n\nDoctor: Do you experience any recurring, distressing thoughts or worries that you can't control, or feel excessively anxious about everyday things or the future?\n\nPatient: No, I don't really have those kinds of anxious worries or racing thoughts. There is just nothing there anymore.\n\nDoctor: How long have you been feeling this emptiness and lack of energy since your husband's passing?\n\nPatient: Looking back, this numb, shut-down way of living started creeping in during the first year after my husband passed. It has stayed about the same for a little over two years now.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about how your feelings of emptiness and lack of energy have changed or stayed the same over the past two years, and have you experienced any periods where you felt somewhat better or more like your old self?\n\nPatient: It hasn't changed or gotten any better; it's stayed consistently the same heavy, numb way for a little over two years now. I haven't had any periods where I felt like my old self again. It's just been a constant emptiness ever since that first year.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any significant emotional pain or distress in response to reminders of your husband, or have you had difficulty accepting the loss, in addition to the emptiness and lack of energy you've described?\n\nPatient: It's not really a sharp emotional pain or crying; it's more of a heavy, hollow numbness where I just can't care about anything. But in the evenings, I do hear his voice plain as day calling my name or telling me not to trust people, which scares me so much I just freeze up. Otherwise, I just feel completely empty and devoid of any energy.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about hearing your husband's voice, such as how often it happens and if it's always the same things he's saying?\n\nPatient: I hear his voice most days, usually in the evenings coming from the back bedroom or the garden. He sometimes calls my name or tells me not to trust people at the door, and it's been happening regularly for the past few months. It scares me so much that I just sit there and listen to him instead of answering the phone or the doorbell.\n\nDoctor: Do you believe the voice you hear is really your husband's spirit trying to communicate with you, or do you think it might be something else, like your own mind playing a trick on you?\n\nPatient: It sounds so incredibly real, just like he is actually right there in the back bedroom or out in the garden. Even though I know the room is physically empty, it is so convincing that I honestly don't know what to believe—whether it is his spirit or my mind playing tricks on me. It just scares me so much that I end up just sitting there and listening to him.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any other unusual perceptions, such as seeing things that aren't there or feeling like someone is touching you when no one is around, in addition to hearing your husband's voice?\n\nPatient: No, I've never seen anything that isn't there or felt anyone touching me. It is strictly just hearing my husband's voice, either calling out my name or warning me not to trust the people who come to the door.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever felt like you're doing things or making decisions because the voice you hear is telling you to, or does the voice just scare you without influencing your actions?\n\nPatient: Yes, his voice definitely influences what I do because it makes me too scared to act. When he tells me not to trust people at the door, it frightens me so much that I just sit there and listen to him. Because of that, I end up completely avoiding answering the phone or the doorbell when they ring.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the voice you hear is a part of your own thoughts or something separate from you, and do you feel like you have control over whether or not you hear it?\n\nPatient: It feels completely separate from my own thoughts, sounding plain as day like he is actually speaking to me from the back bedroom or the garden. I don't have any control over when it happens or what he says. It scares me so much that I just sit there and listen to him.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any other breaks from reality, such as believing things that aren't true or feeling like you're in danger when you're not, aside from hearing your husband's voice?\n\nPatient: No, I don't have any other beliefs like that, and I don't feel like I'm in danger. It's just that his voice tells me not to trust people who come to the door, which scares me so much that I just sit there and ignore the phone or the doorbell.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had any periods where the voice stopped or you didn't hear it for a while, or has it been consistently present over the past few months?\n\nPatient: No, it hasn't stopped at all. It has been very regular and consistent over the past few months, and I hear him most days, especially in the evenings. It has just been a constant presence recently rather than something that comes and goes.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever heard your husband's voice telling you to do something that could potentially harm yourself or others, or has it only been warning you about trusting people?\n\nPatient: No, he has never told me to hurt myself or anyone else. He only calls my name, talks from the back bedroom or the garden, or tells me not to trust people who come to the door. It just scares me so much that I end up sitting there and not doing anything.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever felt like the voice you hear is trying to control your actions or make you do things against your will, rather than just scaring you or giving you warnings?\n\nPatient: No, the voice doesn't try to force me or control me against my will. It is exactly like you said—he mostly just warns me not to trust people at the door, and it scares me so badly that I just freeze up and listen to him instead of answering the phone or the door.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any other types of hallucinations, such as smelling or tasting things that aren't there, in addition to hearing your husband's voice?\n\nPatient: No, I have never smelled or tasted anything unusual that wasn't really there. The only thing like that I experience is hearing my late husband's voice.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe any situations or events that trigger the voice of your husband or make it louder or clearer, and are there any times of the day or specific activities when you're less likely to hear it?\n\nPatient: It seems like a big trigger is when the phone rings or someone comes to the door, because that's when he starts telling me not to trust people. I'm not really sure if there are times I'm less likely to hear it, but it mostly occupies my evenings and just scares me into sitting there and listening. It is all just so tiring and frightening.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the voice you hear is something that would go away if you were distracted or engaged in an activity you enjoy, or does it persist regardless of what you're doing?\n\nPatient: I'm not really sure because I can't bring myself to do the activities I used to enjoy anymore. When I do hear his voice, it scares me so much that I just end up sitting there frozen and listening to it, making it impossible to distract myself or even answer the door or phone.\n\nDoctor: Do you think that the voice you hear is a direct result of your grief over your husband's passing, or does it feel like a separate issue that you're experiencing?\n\nPatient: While his voice started after he passed, it really feels like more than just grief now. It's been happening regularly for the past few months, and him telling me not to trust people at the door scares me so much. It just feels very different from normal grieving.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had any periods where you didn't hear the voice for a while, or has it been consistently present since it started, and are there any other symptoms like this voice that you've experienced?\n\nPatient: The voice has been very regular, happening most days, especially in the evenings for the past few months rather than coming and going. Other than that, I get 'stuck' standing still in the kitchen or hallway for long stretches, or I catch myself pacing back and forth while mumbling prayers under my breath.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about getting 'stuck' standing still in the kitchen or hallway, or pacing back and forth while mumbling prayers, like how often this happens and if it's related to hearing your husband's voice?"

I just don't have any energy or drive to do anything anymore.\n\nDoctor: Do you experience any recurring, distressing thoughts or worries that you can't control, or feel excessively anxious about everyday things or the future?\n\nPatient: No, I don't really have those kinds of anxious worries or racing thoughts. It's more that I just feel completely shut down, empty, and numb inside. There is just nothing there anymore.\n\nDoctor: How long have you been feeling this emptiness and lack of energy since your husband's passing?\n\nPatient: Looking back, this numb, shut-down way of living started creeping in during the first year after my husband passed. It has stayed about the same for a little over two years now.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about how your feelings of emptiness and lack of energy have changed or stayed the same over the past two years, and have you experienced any periods where you felt somewhat better or more like your old self?\n\nPatient: It hasn't changed or gotten any better; it's stayed consistently the same heavy, numb way for a little over two years now. I haven't had any periods where I felt like my old self again. It's just been a constant emptiness ever since that first year.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any significant emotional pain or distress in response to reminders of your husband, or have you had difficulty accepting the loss, in addition to the emptiness and lack of energy you've described?\n\nPatient: It's not really a sharp emotional pain or crying; it's more of a heavy, hollow numbness where I just can't care about anything. Otherwise, I just feel completely empty and devoid of any energy.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about hearing your husband's voice, such as how often it happens and if it's always the same things he's saying?\n\nPatient: I hear his voice most days, usually in the evenings coming from the back bedroom or the garden. He sometimes calls my name or tells me not to trust people at the door, and it's been happening regularly for the past few months. It scares me so much that I just sit there and listen to him instead of answering the phone or the doorbell.\n\nDoctor: Do you believe the voice you hear is really your husband's spirit trying to communicate with you, or do you think it might be something else, like your own mind playing a trick on you?\n\nPatient: It sounds so incredibly real, just like he is actually right there in the back bedroom or out in the garden. Even though I know the room is physically empty, it is so convincing that I honestly don't know what to believe—whether it is his spirit or my mind playing tricks on me. It just scares me so much that I end up just sitting there and listening to him.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any other unusual perceptions, such as seeing things that aren't there or feeling like someone is touching you when no one is around, in addition to hearing your husband's voice?\n\nPatient: No, I've never seen anything that isn't there or felt anyone touching me. It is strictly just hearing my husband's voice, either calling out my name or warning me not to trust the people who come to the door.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever felt like you're doing things or making decisions because the voice you hear is telling you to, or does the voice just scare you without influencing your actions?\n\nPatient: Yes, his voice definitely influences what I do because it makes me too scared to act. Because of that, I end up completely avoiding answering the phone or the doorbell when they ring.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the voice you hear is a part of your own thoughts or something separate from you, and do you feel like you have control over whether or not you hear it?\n\nPatient: It feels completely separate from my own thoughts, sounding plain as day like he is actually speaking to me from the back bedroom or the garden. I don't have any control over when it happens or what he says. It scares me so much that I just sit there and listen to him.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any other breaks from reality, such as believing things that aren't true or feeling like you're in danger when you're not, aside from hearing your husband's voice?\n\nPatient: No, I don't have any other beliefs like that, and I don't feel like I'm in danger. It's just that his voice tells me not to trust people who come to the door, which scares me so much that I just sit there and ignore the phone or the doorbell.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had any periods where the voice stopped or you didn't hear it for a while, or has it been consistently present over the past few months?\n\nPatient: No, it hasn't stopped at all. It has been very regular and consistent over the past few months, and I hear him most days, especially in the evenings. It has just been a constant presence recently rather than something that comes and goes.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever heard your husband's voice telling you to do something that could potentially harm yourself or others, or has it only been warning you about trusting people?\n\nPatient: No, he has never told me to hurt myself or anyone else. He only calls my name, talks from the back bedroom or the garden, or tells me not to trust people who come to the door. It just scares me so much that I end up sitting there and not doing anything.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever felt like the voice you hear is trying to control your actions or make you do things against your will, rather than just scaring you or giving you warnings?\n\nPatient: No, the voice doesn't try to force me or control me against my will. It is exactly like you said—he mostly just warns me not to trust people at the door, and it scares me so badly that I just freeze up and listen to him instead of answering the phone or the door.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any other types of hallucinations, such as smelling or tasting things that aren't there, in addition to hearing your husband's voice?\n\nPatient: No, I have never smelled or tasted anything unusual that wasn't really there. The only thing like that I experience is hearing my late husband's voice.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe any situations or events that trigger the voice of your husband or make it louder or clearer, and are there any times of the day or specific activities when you're less likely to hear it?\n\nPatient: It seems like a big trigger is when the phone rings or someone comes to the door, because that's when he starts telling me not to trust people. I'm not really sure if there are times I'm less likely to hear it, but it mostly occupies my evenings and just scares me into sitting there and listening. It is all just so tiring and frightening.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the voice you hear is something that would go away if you were distracted or engaged in an activity you enjoy, or does it persist regardless of what you're doing?\n\nPatient: I'm not really sure because I can't bring myself to do the activities I used to enjoy anymore. When I do hear his voice, it scares me so much that I just end up sitting there frozen and listening to it, making it impossible to distract myself or even answer the door or phone.\n\nDoctor: Do you think that the voice you hear is a direct result of your grief over your husband's passing, or does it feel like a separate issue that you're experiencing?\n\nPatient: While his voice started after he passed, it really feels like more than just grief now. It just feels very different from normal grieving.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had any periods where you didn't hear the voice for a while, or has it been consistently present since it started, and are there any other symptoms like this voice that you've experienced?\n\nPatient: The voice has been very regular, happening most days, especially in the evenings for the past few months rather than coming and going. Other than that, I get 'stuck' standing still in the kitchen or hallway for long stretches, or I catch myself pacing back and forth while mumbling prayers under my breath.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about getting 'stuck' standing still in the kitchen or hallway, or pacing back and forth while mumbling prayers, like how often this happens and if it's related to hearing your husband's voice?\n\nPatient: My daughter is usually the one who notices me standing completely still in the kitchen or hallway holding a dish or some mail, and I also find myself pacing and mumbling prayers regularly these past few months. These things feel separate from hearing my husband's voice, though; the pacing and standing happen almost unconsciously for no clear reason, while his voice in the evenings makes me freeze up out of pure fear just to listen to him.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the voice you hear and the feelings of emptiness and numbness are connected, or do they feel like two separate things that are happening to you?\n\nPatient: I haven't really thought about whether they are connected or separate, but both seemed to take over after my husband passed away. The emptiness is like a constant, heavy weight all the time, while hearing his voice is frightening and mostly happens in the evenings. I'm just not sure if they are truly linked.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the voice you hear is more distressing to you, or is the feeling of emptiness and lack of energy more bothersome in your daily life?\n\nPatient: Hearing my husband's voice is terrifying and makes me freeze in fear, but the emptiness and feeling of being shut down is what has completely taken over my life. They are both heavy burdens, but that lack of drive is what keeps me stuck in the dark day after day and stops me from doing anything I used to love.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the voice you hear is something that would improve if your feelings of emptiness and numbness improved, or do you think it's a completely separate issue that needs to be addressed on its own?"

It just scares me so much that I end up just sitting there and listening to him.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any other unusual perceptions, such as seeing things that aren't there or feeling like someone is touching you when no one is around, in addition to hearing your husband's voice?\n\nPatient: No, I've never seen anything that isn't there or felt anyone touching me. It is strictly just hearing my husband's voice, either calling out my name or warning me not to trust the people who come to the door.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever felt like you're doing things or making decisions because the voice you hear is telling you to, or does the voice just scare you without influencing your actions?\n\nPatient: Yes, his voice definitely influences what I do because it makes me too scared to act. When he tells me not to trust people at the door, it frightens me so much that I just sit there and listen to him. Because of that, I end up completely avoiding answering the phone or the doorbell when they ring.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the voice you hear is a part of your own thoughts or something separate from you, and do you feel like you have control over whether or not you hear it?\n\nPatient: It feels completely separate from my own thoughts, sounding plain as day like he is actually speaking to me from the back bedroom or the garden. I don't have any control over when it happens or what he says. It scares me so much that I just sit there and listen to him.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any other breaks from reality, such as believing things that aren't true or feeling like you're in danger when you're not, aside from hearing your husband's voice?\n\nPatient: No, I don't have any other beliefs like that, and I don't feel like I'm in danger. It's just that his voice tells me not to trust people who come to the door, which scares me so much that I just sit there and ignore the phone or the doorbell.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had any periods where the voice stopped or you didn't hear it for a while, or has it been consistently present over the past few months?\n\nPatient: No, it hasn't stopped at all. It has been very regular and consistent over the past few months, and I hear him most days, especially in the evenings. It has just been a constant presence recently rather than something that comes and goes.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever heard your husband's voice telling you to do something that could potentially harm yourself or others, or has it only been warning you about trusting people?\n\nPatient: No, he has never told me to hurt myself or anyone else. He only calls my name, talks from the back bedroom or the garden, or tells me not to trust people who come to the door. It just scares me so much that I end up sitting there and not doing anything.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever felt like the voice you hear is trying to control your actions or make you do things against your will, rather than just scaring you or giving you warnings?\n\nPatient: No, the voice doesn't try to force me or control me against my will. It is exactly like you said—he mostly just warns me not to trust people at the door, and it scares me so badly that I just freeze up and listen to him instead of answering the phone or the door.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any other types of hallucinations, such as smelling or tasting things that aren't there, in addition to hearing your husband's voice?\n\nPatient: No, I have never smelled or tasted anything unusual that wasn't really there. The only thing like that I experience is hearing my late husband's voice.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe any situations or events that trigger the voice of your husband or make it louder or clearer, and are there any times of the day or specific activities when you're less likely to hear it?\n\nPatient: It seems like a big trigger is when the phone rings or someone comes to the door, because that's when he starts telling me not to trust people. I'm not really sure if there are times I'm less likely to hear it, but it mostly occupies my evenings and just scares me into sitting there and listening. It is all just so tiring and frightening.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the voice you hear is something that would go away if you were distracted or engaged in an activity you enjoy, or does it persist regardless of what you're doing?\n\nPatient: I'm not really sure because I can't bring myself to do the activities I used to enjoy anymore. When I do hear his voice, it scares me so much that I just end up sitting there frozen and listening to it, making it impossible to distract myself or even answer the door or phone.\n\nDoctor: Do you think that the voice you hear is a direct result of your grief over your husband's passing, or does it feel like a separate issue that you're experiencing?\n\nPatient: While his voice started after he passed, it really feels like more than just grief now. It's been happening regularly for the past few months, and him telling me not to trust people at the door scares me so much. It just feels very different from normal grieving.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had any periods where you didn't hear the voice for a while, or has it been consistently present since it started, and are there any other symptoms like this voice that you've experienced?\n\nPatient: The voice has been very regular, happening most days, especially in the evenings for the past few months rather than coming and going. Other than that, I get 'stuck' standing still in the kitchen or hallway for long stretches, or I catch myself pacing back and forth while mumbling prayers under my breath.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about getting 'stuck' standing still in the kitchen or hallway, or pacing back and forth while mumbling prayers, like how often this happens and if it's related to hearing your husband's voice?\n\nPatient: My daughter is usually the one who notices me standing completely still in the kitchen or hallway holding a dish or some mail, and I also find myself pacing and mumbling prayers regularly these past few months. These things feel separate from hearing my husband's voice, though; the pacing and standing happen almost unconsciously for no clear reason, while his voice in the evenings makes me freeze up out of pure fear just to listen to him.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the voice you hear and the feelings of emptiness and numbness are connected, or do they feel like two separate things that are happening to you?\n\nPatient: I haven't really thought about whether they are connected or separate, but both seemed to take over after my husband passed away. The emptiness is like a constant, heavy weight all the time, while hearing his voice is frightening and mostly happens in the evenings. I'm just not sure if they are truly linked.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the voice you hear is more distressing to you, or is the feeling of emptiness and lack of energy more bothersome in your daily life?\n\nPatient: Hearing my husband's voice is terrifying and makes me freeze in fear, but the emptiness and feeling of being shut down is what has completely taken over my life. They are both heavy burdens, but that lack of drive is what keeps me stuck in the dark day after day and stops me from doing anything I used to love.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the voice you hear is something that would improve if your feelings of emptiness and numbness improved, or do you think it's a completely separate issue that needs to be addressed on its own?\n\nPatient: I'm really not sure if one would go away with the other. Since they both started after my husband passed, they feel all tangled together in my mind. I just don't know if treating the numbness would make the voice stop or if they are separate issues."

It scares me so much that I just sit there and listen to him.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any other breaks from reality, such as believing things that aren't true or feeling like you're in danger when you're not, aside from hearing your husband's voice?\n\nPatient: No, I don't have any other beliefs like that, and I don't feel like I'm in danger. It's just that his voice tells me not to trust people who come to the door, which scares me so much that I just sit there and ignore the phone or the doorbell.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had any periods where the voice stopped or you didn't hear it for a while, or has it been consistently present over the past few months?\n\nPatient: No, it hasn't stopped at all. It has been very regular and consistent over the past few months, and I hear him most days, especially in the evenings. It has just been a constant presence recently rather than something that comes and goes.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever heard your husband's voice telling you to do something that could potentially harm yourself or others, or has it only been warning you about trusting people?\n\nPatient: No, he has never told me to hurt myself or anyone else. He only calls my name, talks from the back bedroom or the garden, or tells me not to trust people who come to the door. It just scares me so much that I end up sitting there and not doing anything.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever felt like the voice you hear is trying to control your actions or make you do things against your will, rather than just scaring you or giving you warnings?\n\nPatient: No, the voice doesn't try to force me or control me against my will. It is exactly like you said—he mostly just warns me not to trust people at the door, and it scares me so badly that I just freeze up and listen to him instead of answering the phone or the door.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any other types of hallucinations, such as smelling or tasting things that aren't there, in addition to hearing your husband's voice?\n\nPatient: No, I have never smelled or tasted anything unusual that wasn't really there. The only thing like that I experience is hearing my late husband's voice.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe any situations or events that trigger the voice of your husband or make it louder or clearer, and are there any times of the day or specific activities when you're less likely to hear it?\n\nPatient: It seems like a big trigger is when the phone rings or someone comes to the door, because that's when he starts telling me not to trust people. I'm not really sure if there are times I'm less likely to hear it, but it mostly occupies my evenings and just scares me into sitting there and listening. It is all just so tiring and frightening.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the voice you hear is something that would go away if you were distracted or engaged in an activity you enjoy, or does it persist regardless of what you're doing?\n\nPatient: I'm not really sure because I can't bring myself to do the activities I used to enjoy anymore. When I do hear his voice, it scares me so much that I just end up sitting there frozen and listening to it, making it impossible to distract myself or even answer the door or phone.\n\nDoctor: Do you think that the voice you hear is a direct result of your grief over your husband's passing, or does it feel like a separate issue that you're experiencing?\n\nPatient: While his voice started after he passed, it really feels like more than just grief now. Other than that, I get 'stuck' standing still in the kitchen or hallway for long stretches, or I catch myself pacing back and forth while mumbling prayers under my breath.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about getting 'stuck' standing still in the kitchen or hallway, or pacing back and forth while mumbling prayers, like how often this happens and if it's related to hearing your husband's voice?\n\nPatient: My daughter is usually the one who notices me standing completely still in the kitchen or hallway holding a dish or some mail, and I also find myself pacing and mumbling prayers regularly these past few months. These things feel separate from hearing my husband's voice, though; the pacing and standing happen almost unconsciously for no clear reason, while his voice in the evenings makes me freeze up out of pure fear just to listen to him.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the voice you hear and the feelings of emptiness and numbness are connected, or do they feel like two separate things that are happening to you?\n\nPatient: I haven't really thought about whether they are connected or separate, but both seemed to take over after my husband passed away. The emptiness is like a constant, heavy weight all the time, while hearing his voice is frightening and mostly happens in the evenings. I'm just not sure if they are truly linked.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the voice you hear is more distressing to you, or is the feeling of emptiness and lack of energy more bothersome in your daily life?\n\nPatient: Hearing my husband's voice is terrifying and makes me freeze in fear, but the emptiness and feeling of being shut down is what has completely taken over my life. They are both heavy burdens, but that lack of drive is what keeps me stuck in the dark day after day and stops me from doing anything I used to love.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the voice you hear is something that would improve if your feelings of emptiness and numbness improved, or do you think it's a completely separate issue that needs to be addressed on its own?\n\nPatient: I'm really not sure if one would go away with the other. Since they both started after my husband passed, they feel all tangled together in my mind. I just don't know if treating the numbness would make the voice stop or if they are separate issues.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any other types of unusual thoughts or behaviors, such as feeling like you're being watched or having thoughts that don't seem like your own, in addition to hearing your husband's voice and feeling empty and numb?\n\nPatient: No, I don't feel like I'm being watched or like thoughts are being put into my head. All I know is that his voice feels incredibly real to me, like he is actually right there in the room. It is just so frightening, and it feels completely out of my control."

But in the evenings, I do hear his voice plain as day calling my name or telling me not to trust people, which scares me so much I just freeze up. Otherwise, I just feel completely empty and devoid of any energy.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about hearing your husband's voice, such as how often it happens and if it's always the same things he's saying?\n\nPatient: I hear his voice most days, usually in the evenings coming from the back bedroom or the garden. He sometimes calls my name or tells me not to trust people at the door, and it's been happening regularly for the past few months. It scares me so much that I just sit there and listen to him instead of answering the phone or the doorbell.\n\nDoctor: Do you believe the voice you hear is really your husband's spirit trying to communicate with you, or do you think it might be something else, like your own mind playing a trick on you?\n\nPatient: It sounds so incredibly real, just like he is actually right there in the back bedroom or out in the garden. Even though I know the room is physically empty, it is so convincing that I honestly don't know what to believe—whether it is his spirit or my mind playing tricks on me. It just scares me so much that I end up just sitting there and listening to him.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any other unusual perceptions, such as seeing things that aren't there or feeling like someone is touching you when no one is around, in addition to hearing your husband's voice?\n\nPatient: No, I've never seen anything that isn't there or felt anyone touching me. It is strictly just hearing my husband's voice, either calling out my name or warning me not to trust the people who come to the door.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever felt like you're doing things or making decisions because the voice you hear is telling you to, or does the voice just scare you without influencing your actions?\n\nPatient: Yes, his voice definitely influences what I do because it makes me too scared to act. When he tells me not to trust people at the door, it frightens me so much that I just sit there and listen to him. Because of that, I end up completely avoiding answering the phone or the doorbell when they ring.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the voice you hear is a part of your own thoughts or something separate from you, and do you feel like you have control over whether or not you hear it?\n\nPatient: It feels completely separate from my own thoughts, sounding plain as day like he is actually speaking to me from the back bedroom or the garden. I don't have any control over when it happens or what he says. It scares me so much that I just sit there and listen to him.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any other breaks from reality, such as believing things that aren't true or feeling like you're in danger when you're not, aside from hearing your husband's voice?\n\nPatient: No, I don't have any other beliefs like that, and I don't feel like I'm in danger. It's just that his voice tells me not to trust people who come to the door, which scares me so much that I just sit there and ignore the phone or the doorbell.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had any periods where the voice stopped or you didn't hear it for a while, or has it been consistently present over the past few months?\n\nPatient: No, it hasn't stopped at all. It has been very regular and consistent over the past few months, and I hear him most days, especially in the evenings. It has just been a constant presence recently rather than something that comes and goes.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever heard your husband's voice telling you to do something that could potentially harm yourself or others, or has it only been warning you about trusting people?\n\nPatient: No, he has never told me to hurt myself or anyone else. He only calls my name, talks from the back bedroom or the garden, or tells me not to trust people who come to the door. It just scares me so much that I end up sitting there and not doing anything.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever felt like the voice you hear is trying to control your actions or make you do things against your will, rather than just scaring you or giving you warnings?\n\nPatient: No, the voice doesn't try to force me or control me against my will. The only thing like that I experience is hearing my late husband's voice.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe any situations or events that trigger the voice of your husband or make it louder or clearer, and are there any times of the day or specific activities when you're less likely to hear it?\n\nPatient: It seems like a big trigger is when the phone rings or someone comes to the door, because that's when he starts telling me not to trust people. It is all just so tiring and frightening.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the voice you hear is something that would go away if you were distracted or engaged in an activity you enjoy, or does it persist regardless of what you're doing?\n\nPatient: I'm not really sure because I can't bring myself to do the activities I used to enjoy anymore. When I do hear his voice, it scares me so much that I just end up sitting there frozen and listening to it, making it impossible to distract myself or even answer the door or phone.\n\nDoctor: Do you think that the voice you hear is a direct result of your grief over your husband's passing, or does it feel like a separate issue that you're experiencing?\n\nPatient: While his voice started after he passed, it really feels like more than just grief now. It's been happening regularly for the past few months, and him telling me not to trust people at the door scares me so much. It just feels very different from normal grieving.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had any periods where you didn't hear the voice for a while, or has it been consistently present since it started, and are there any other symptoms like this voice that you've experienced?\n\nPatient: The voice has been very regular, happening most days, especially in the evenings for the past few months rather than coming and going. Other than that, I get 'stuck' standing still in the kitchen or hallway for long stretches, or I catch myself pacing back and forth while mumbling prayers under my breath.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about getting 'stuck' standing still in the kitchen or hallway, or pacing back and forth while mumbling prayers, like how often this happens and if it's related to hearing your husband's voice?\n\nPatient: My daughter is usually the one who notices me standing completely still in the kitchen or hallway holding a dish or some mail, and I also find myself pacing and mumbling prayers regularly these past few months. These things feel separate from hearing my husband's voice, though; the pacing and standing happen almost unconsciously for no clear reason, while his voice in the evenings makes me freeze up out of pure fear just to listen to him.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the voice you hear and the feelings of emptiness and numbness are connected, or do they feel like two separate things that are happening to you?\n\nPatient: I haven't really thought about whether they are connected or separate, but both seemed to take over after my husband passed away. The emptiness is like a constant, heavy weight all the time, while hearing his voice is frightening and mostly happens in the evenings. I'm just not sure if they are truly linked.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the voice you hear is more distressing to you, or is the feeling of emptiness and lack of energy more bothersome in your daily life?\n\nPatient: Hearing my husband's voice is terrifying and makes me freeze in fear, but the emptiness and feeling of being shut down is what has completely taken over my life. They are both heavy burdens, but that lack of drive is what keeps me stuck in the dark day after day and stops me from doing anything I used to love.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the voice you hear is something that would improve if your feelings of emptiness and numbness improved, or do you think it's a completely separate issue that needs to be addressed on its own?\n\nPatient: I'm really not sure if one would go away with the other. I just don't know if treating the numbness would make the voice stop or if they are separate issues.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any other types of unusual thoughts or behaviors, such as feeling like you're being watched or having thoughts that don't seem like your own, in addition to hearing your husband's voice and feeling empty and numb?\n\nPatient: No, I don't feel like I'm being watched or like thoughts are being put into my head.
